title: 0PN companion momentum, towing and driven acceleration through a renewing shear contact
scope: Exploratory fixed-chart transport model. One isolated flared carrier supplies the clocks, one separately computed paired-minus-alone feeding field supplies the incident momentum. Unit mass per participating constituent. No fitted Newton force, bare mouth mass or free-release solution.

conventions.held: Positive toward companion. Rim, surrounding brane and output are distinct endpoints. The holder reaction is opposite to the material force on the rim.
conventions.acceleration: The coefficient printed is the signed actuator force derivative with respect to slow acceleration, at fixed instantaneous velocity, in resting feeding material. Harmonic convention exp(+i omega t). Includes age distribution. No added bare mass.
conventions.support: Surrounding support is fixed or massless with a real, frequency-independent resistance. Free denotes vanishing force on this support. Physical mouth release is a separate experiment.
conventions.numerical_checks: Three feeding grids, two aperture quadratures, two throat meshes, alternate contact schedules/mobility, signed steady mixed drive, ray momentum and work budgets, acceleration and two harmonic drives. Archived physical array digests were compared at assembly and in the solvers.

dispositions: The two charts and projected tangent directions are supplied, with no common paired phase solution or response of the carrier to rim motion. Absolute contact law and conversion depth are assumptions.
Towing is a steady control. Acceleration results are slow driven susceptibilities, not instantaneous release mass. Static support impedance alone does not determine its dynamic response.
The acceleration runs check the total force, storage and export identity per ray. They record the residual, not a numerical split of stored and exported momentum under acceleration.
Finite frequencies check the reactive slope within the same material model. The two mesh thresholds are numerical readings, not a validated continuum interval.
